mcqs.question: A student draws three lines on paper and thinks that because the lines intersect, they must all meet at a single point. Which statement correctly addresses this misconception?

options.A: All three lines always intersect at one common point.
options.B: Only if the three lines are concurrent will they meet at one point; otherwise they can intersect pairwise at different points.
options.C: Three lines can never intersect each other.
options.D: If two lines intersect, the third line must be parallel to one of them.

mcqs.answer: Only if the three lines are concurrent will they meet at one point; otherwise they can intersect pairwise at different points.
mcqs.explanation: Three lines are said to be concurrent only when they all pass through the same point. In general, each pair of lines can intersect at a different point, giving up to three distinct intersection points. Options A, C and D are false statements.

mcqs.question: Line L1 meets line L2 at point P, and line L2 meets line L3 at point Q. Which point is the intersection of line L1 and line L3?

options.C: A new point R distinct from P and Q
options.D: The lines L1 and L3 do not intersect

mcqs.answer: A new point R distinct from P and Q
mcqs.explanation: Since P is the intersection of L1 and L2, and Q is the intersection of L2 and L3, there is no information that L1 and L3 share either of those points. If the three lines are not concurrent, L1 and L3 will intersect at a third point, call it R. Therefore option C is correct; A and B incorrectly reuse existing points, and D is false because two non‑parallel lines always intersect.

mcqs.question: In configuration A, three lines intersect at a point forming angles of 30°, 60°, and 90° among the acute angles. In configuration B, the same three lines intersect at a corresponding point forming acute angles of 45°, 75°, and 60°. Which configuration has the largest acute angle?

options.C: Both configurations have the same largest acute angle
options.D: Neither configuration has an acute angle

mcqs.explanation: The largest acute angle in configuration A is 60°, while in configuration B it is 75°. Since 75° > 60°, configuration B possesses the larger acute angle. Options A and C are therefore incorrect, and D is false because both configurations contain acute angles.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes a situation where three lines intersect such that each pair meets at a different point, forming a small triangle in the middle?

options.A: Three concurrent lines meeting at a single point
options.C: Three lines intersecting pairwise at three distinct points, creating a central triangle
options.D: Two lines intersect and the third line is parallel to one of them

mcqs.answer: Three lines intersecting pairwise at three distinct points, creating a central triangle
mcqs.explanation: When each pair of lines meets at a separate point, the three intersection points become the vertices of a small triangle bounded by the three lines. This matches option C. Options A and B describe configurations without separate intersection points, and D does not give three distinct intersections.

mcqs.question: Which picture correctly shows three lines that intersect each other at three distinct points?

options.A: All three lines meet at one common point
options.B: Two lines are parallel and the third crosses both of them
options.C: Each line crosses the other two at different points, giving three separate intersections

mcqs.answer: Each line crosses the other two at different points, giving three separate intersections
mcqs.explanation: Option C depicts the required configuration: three lines, each intersecting the other two at different locations, resulting in three distinct intersection points. Option A shows concurrency, B shows only two intersections, and D shows no intersections.

mcqs.question: If three lines intersect pairwise but no three are concurrent, how many distinct intersection points are there?
mcqs.explanation: Each pair of lines gives one intersection point. With three lines, there are three pairs (L1‑L2, L1‑L3, L2‑L3), so three distinct intersection points arise when the lines are not concurrent. Hence option C is correct; the other numbers are too few.

mcqs.question: The angle formed between two intersecting lines is called:
mcqs.explanation: When two lines cross, the space between them is measured as an angle. 'Vertex' is the point of intersection, 'side' and 'segment' refer to parts of a line or shape, not the measure between lines. Therefore, option C is correct.

mcqs.question: In a city map, three roads cross each other such that each road meets the other two at different junctions, creating a small triangular block. Which description matches this arrangement?

options.A: All three roads meet at a roundabout
options.B: Two roads are parallel and the third cuts across them
options.C: Each road intersects the other two at separate points, forming a triangle
options.D: One road ends in a dead‑end while the other two intersect

mcqs.answer: Each road intersects the other two at separate points, forming a triangle
mcqs.explanation: The described situation is exactly a set of three lines intersecting pairwise at three distinct points, which outlines a triangular region. Option C captures this; A describes concurrency, B gives only two intersections, and D does not involve three intersecting lines.
